result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder. I haven't added a test for the new cases, and I didn't run `x-pack/plugin/inference/qa/test-service-plugin/.../inference/mock/` or the other new cases (`mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/`) through the rule. The scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` still pass.

In `ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394) I replaced the two mock-folder regexes, which only allowed `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` after `mock`:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`.
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

By the regex, a plain `mock/` folder now matches, as do names with punctuation or non-ASCII characters after `mock`. The match stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` still don't match. All the folder types that were test before still match.

Backslash paths work because `SourceFileFilter.matches` normalizes `\` to `/` before matching.
